item.description:
Last authors: J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

Authors: D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of phonon-magnon coupling in magnetic thin films.

Tags: #experiment #magnetism #thin-film #magnon #phonon

Abstract: Author(s): D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard FeRh is best known for its metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction. Here, the authors reveal remarkably strong phonon–magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh. Combining Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling, they demonstrate giant magnetoelasticity and show that Love surface acoustic waves provide an efficient mechanism for coherent magnon-polaron formation in magnetic thin films, highlighting FeRh as a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing. Tags: #theory #superconductivity #twisted-bilayer #cuprate #TRSB

Abstract: Author(s): Siddhant Panda, Andreas Kreisel, Laura Fanfarillo, and P. J. Hirschfeld Twisted cuprate Josephson junctions have been proposed as candidate platforms for superconducting states that break time-reversal symmetry. However, experiments report conflicting signatures. Here, the authors show that this variability can arise from microscopic parameters: the systematic exploration of the phase diagram reveals that twist angle θ, filling, and interlayer tunneling strength stabilize distinct competing superconducting states.
